sets.title: A short history of photography
text: Photography has had great {{1}} for how people remember events. Early cameras were large and {{2}} to carry around.
Several {{3}} in camera technology changed this during the twentieth century. Many photographers now work {{4}} for newspapers and magazines.
Good {{5}} often matters more than expensive equipment, and a single photograph can have a {{6}} effect on how we see history.
Modern phones can now match equipment that used to be extremely {{7}}. Some experts worry that people now take photographs too {{8}}, without thinking about the moment.

questions.explanation: The negative prefix 'in-' is needed because large cameras were difficult, not easy, to carry.
The adverb 'professionally' is needed to describe how the photographers work.
'Timing' is the noun formed from 'time' meaning the choice of the right moment.
The adjective 'powerful' is needed to describe the effect of the photograph.
The adjective 'expensive' is needed after the linking verb 'to be'.
The adverb 'carelessly' describes the manner of taking photographs without much thought.
